record.title: STMicroelectronics ST25R3916 — high performance NFC universal device and EMVCo reader (reader/writer, card emulation, P2P; SPI or I2C host), VFQFPN32 / UFQFPN32 5x5 mm
record.why: IDENTITY READ OFF THE VENDOR'S OWN DOCUMENT. datasheet.pdf is ST's DS12484 Rev 8 fetched 2026-09-02 from st.com (HTTP 200, 2241765 bytes, sha256 in PROVENANCE.json); p.1 prints verbatim 'May 2023 DS12484 Rev 8 1/160' and 'Datasheet - production data'. Every figure in electrical.chip.json is quoted from it. WHAT THIS FOLDER IS: an NFC READER-IC CANDIDATE for the Microduck's two NFC antennas ('one in the head and one in the beak', press kit). THE FITTED NFC IC IS CANNOT DETERMINE — no NFC code exists in the published runtime and the HAT is unpublished (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §8). The sheet's own feature 'Possibility to drive two independent single ended antennas' is why this candidate is on the shelf next to part:pn7150. PASS means the part is exactly identified and its sheet is here; it does not claim the part is fitted.
record.subsector_why: open vocabulary; the sheet's own words: 'High performance NFC universal device and EMVCo reader'.
record.lifecycle_why: the datasheet is marked 'Datasheet - production data' (May 2023); ST's product page was not fetched, so 'active' rests on that marking alone.
record.origin_why: the manufacturer's own datasheet PDF was FETCHED from st.com and saved byte for byte as datasheet.pdf; PROVENANCE.json carries its sha256, size and URL.
record.standards_why: AS CLAIMED BY THE DATASHEET, not verified here: p.1 'NFC-A / ISO14443A up to 848 kbit/s', 'NFC-B / ISO14443B up to 848 kbit/s', 'NFC-V / ISO15693 up to 53 kb/s', 'EMVCo 3.0 analog and digital compliant', and p.1 'ISO 18092 passive and active initiator'. These are protocol standards the chip implements; they are not a dimensional standard that makes this a catalogue part, and there is no sourced offer — T4 is not earned and not claimed (TRIAD.md). The ledger's `standard` row records the same claim with the same caveat.
record.used_by_why: no ce-elec board in this design names it; the HAT is the place an NFC reader would sit.
